title: Automatic account deletion backend readiness
requestedBehavior: An authenticated deletion request sets a 168-hour deadline. If not cancelled before expiry, scheduled execution processes the eligible request without requiring another user login.

implementedNow.body: Empty; any body or query is rejected. No userId, requestId, date or force parameter.
implementedNow.authentication: Google-signed ID token in Authorization: Bearer. Pinned audience, numeric service-account sub and verified service-account email; signature, issuer, expiry and issued-at checked. Admin JWTs and user sessions cannot authorize the trigger.
implementedNow.execution: Synchronous HTTP work, not a background task after responding. Uses the existing due-only worker, locks, immutable cleanup plans, storage generations, provider receipts and bounded retries.
implementedNow.batch: At most one eligible account per scheduled invocation. With a one-minute schedule, eligible accounts start on a later tick, subject to backlog, lock contention, safety holds and provider retries; exact wall-clock completion is not guaranteed.
implementedNow.response: 204 acknowledges a cycle, including empty/contended cycles. It does not mean every due account completed. Per-account FAILED/COMPLETED status and last_error remain authoritative. Selection/readiness errors produce 503.
implementedNow.timer: When trigger.enabled=true, the in-process timer does not auto-start. Workers remain default-off.
implementedNow.schema: No new database migration or existing-table change is needed for this patch.

sourceEvidence.finding: Legacy uploadToGcs and legacy archiveRemoteFile use random images/ keys without end-user owner metadata or durable per-user upload history.
meshyTaskId is copied from the client payload. No trusted server-side Meshy task creation is implemented here.
New integration-enabled uploads already reserve server-owned user keys and exact generations. This does not retroactively prove ownership of old images/ objects.
Coverage and historical Meshy task evidence require trusted review/import. No real evidence was invented or imported.

readOnlyDatabaseFindings.existingUserForeignKeys: Only known deletion-module FKs were found. users/accountStatus and meeting data were not modified.

activationBlockers: Legacy images/ ownership and historical Meshy task provenance are not in this backend database; do not infer exclusive ownership from a User URL or client task ID.
The configured backend Meshy credential, allowed cleanup bucket, provider-call approval and shared-meeting/retention policy are still required. Do not copy a Unity-embedded key into logs/source.

All six cleanup review domains, including historical/unlinked objects, provider grants and retained shared data, must be covered. Newly instrumented uploads alone do not establish complete historical coverage.
ACTIVE hosted meetings require an approved resolution; shared recordings/files remain protected.
The new source must be deployed after readiness is established. No Cloud Scheduler job, dedicated service-account identity or IAM binding was created here.
Cloud Run is currently minScale=0 and cpu-throttling=true. The old idle timer is unreliable there. A properly configured authenticated Cloud Scheduler HTTP target is required to use this patch.
Load/failover, real provider permissions, per-account HTTP execution duration, retry exhaustion alerts and backup/retention handling must be verified before unattended destructive activation.

futureDeployment.warning: Instructions only. These are NOT the currently active settings and were NOT applied.
futureDeployment.prerequisites: Reconcile trusted evidence and policy first; keep request status/cancellation and integration available. Do not disable integration or backdate requests.

configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_TRIGGER_AUDIENCE: Exact deployed Cloud Run service URL, matching the scheduler OIDC audience
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_TRIGGER_SERVICEA: Dedicated scheduler service account numeric uniqueId; not a user ID
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_CLEANUP_AUTOMATI: true only after inventory coverage is reviewed
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_CLEANUP_PROVIDER: true only after provider permissions and ownership are verified
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_CLEANUP_ANONYMIZ: true only after structured-reference retention policy is approved
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_ALLOWEDBUCKETS: nukleus-verse-storage only after reviewing storage policy
configurationAfterApproval.NUKLEUS_ACCOUNTDELETION_CLEANUP_MESHYAPI: Secret Manager reference to the correct Meshy application credential, never plaintext in this file

job.identity: Dedicated service-account OIDC token, same exact audience and pinned sub/email as backend configuration
job.retry: Bounded scheduler retries for 503 plus recurring ticks. Per-account retries stay governed by the existing 5-attempt policy.
job.safety: Do not force-run against real accounts, alter stored deadlines, lower the grace period, or provide user IDs. Verify safe request duration within Cloud Run and Scheduler timeouts before activation.

futureDeployment.monitor: Alert on due request backlog, FAILED, retry exhaustion, prolonged PROCESSING, 401/503 trigger responses, and excessive request duration. A 204 alone is not a completion audit.

tests.scope: Isolated loopback PostgreSQL 17, synthetic accounts, MockMvc and locally signed RSA tokens, mocked Storage/Meshy/Google. No Spring Boot production server launched.
